pages.text: Pipo played ball at the hilltop. The ball rolled along, flattening the grass wherever it went.
It disappeared into tall grass below. "It is my only ball. I will find it!" Pipo hurried down.
Without a word, Grandpa pointed his walking stick toward the stream, looking as if he already knew everything.
Grandpa stirred the stream with his stick. Only water weeds came up, dangling.
"In the old days, balls always washed down here." Grandpa splashed into the stream.
This time, an old boot came up. "Oh, is this not my boot?"
Grandpa held the boot upside down. Only water poured out.
Pipo looked back at the hill. Flattened grass made a long path.
The trail ended at a thorn bush. The ball was tucked underneath.
Pipo took it out and hugged it. Grandpa strode over wearing his found boot. "Found the ball and the boot too!"
